In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aided INS with homogeneous features is unobservable in at least four directions, which is independent of the number of features, while for the aided INS with heterogeneous features, the unobservable directions are at least four, which can be reduced if global measurements are provided.

the unobservable subsphere of the aided INS with a combination of heterogeneous geometric features is at most the same as that of the aided INS only with point features, i.e., a subsphere of dimension four.
, for the linearized INS aided by exteroception sensors with geometric features, the system is unobservable in the yaw direction and unobservable in at least one translation direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general (with global measurements), the aided INS with heterogeneous features of points, lines, and planes has at least four unobserved directions, while, without global measurements, it has at least six unobserved directions.

the unobservable subspaces for the general aided INS are the same as those for the VINS with point features, and the number of unobservable directions is the same for the aided INS with homogeneous features as well as with combinations of heterogeneous ones, while the unobservable subsurface for the former is larger than that for the latter.
, for the first order INS, the observability of VINS with point features is preserved for the case of aided INS with point or line (or plane) features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general (except for the special case of a single line feature), aided INS with homogeneous or heterogeneous features preserves the same unobservable subspace as that of VINS with point features.
, in general aided INS with heterogeneous features, there will be four unobservable directions even with global measurements.
, while the addition of geometric features can improve the observability of INS, the unobservable directions are not eliminated, and the system is not fully observable.
